statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F(x,y,z) = 4 x\vec j + 3 y\vec k through the surface S, where S is the part of the surface z=-y+3 above the rectangle 0\le x\le 4, 0\le y\le 2, oriented upward.

static.solution: S as z=f(x,y)=-y + 3, we have d\vec A= (-f_x\vec i - f_y\vec j + \vec k)dxdy = \vec j + \vec k. Thus, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2}\int_0^{4} (4 x\vec j + 3 y\vec k)\cdot (\vec j+\vec k)\,dxdy = \int_0^{2}\int_0^{4} 4 x + 3 y\, dxdy = \int_0^{2} (2 x^2 + 3 xy)\bigg|_0^{4}\,dy = \int_0^{2} (32 + 12 y)\,dy = (32 y + 6 y^2)\bigg|_0^{2}= 88.
